reasons: The cited Section 13 language is a Vendor-side (Garman) indemnity that, in substance, covers third-party IP claims: it warrants ownership of all rights necessary and absence of liens, indemnifies Sparkling for all Losses (settlement amounts, reasonable legal fees) from breach of that warranty, and supplies the customary infringement remedies (procure right, procure equivalent, replace/modify at Vendor's expense). This meets the fallback position, so classifying it as compliant and not redlining is correct under the playbook's classification semantics.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact — the indemnity is framed as breach of the IP ownership/non-infringement warranty rather than using the words 'infringe or misappropriate' — and does not undermine the substantive conclusion.

There is no reciprocal or one-way Customer indemnity anywhere, and Section 15 expressly carves Section 13 out of the damages limitation, so the Vendor indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap and clearly not walk-away territory; flagging would be over-flagging.

Shortfalls versus preferred (no express duty to defend/control the defence, no refund remedy, no extension to breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and a tight ten-day notice period) are correctly recorded in the rationale as noted-but-not-flagged sub-elements rather than raised as deviations.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was applied (redline text is identical to the original) and no counterparty comment was generated, as expected.
